test.title: The layers of a green roof

paragraphs.text: A green roof is a roof covered with living plants. Although it looks simple from above, it is built from several layers, each with its own job.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: At the bottom, directly on the roof structure, is a waterproof membrane that stops water from entering the building. Above it lies a root barrier, which prevents plant roots from damaging the membrane.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The next layer is for drainage. It is often made of plastic panels shaped like egg boxes, which store some rainwater for dry periods and allow the rest to flow away. A thin filter sheet on top keeps soil from blocking the drainage layer.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The plants grow in a lightweight growing medium rather than ordinary soil, which would be too heavy for most roofs. Low-growing plants called sedums are popular because they survive long periods without rain.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Green roofs can also reduce the amount of rainwater that flows into drains during storms and help to keep buildings cooler in summer.
paragraphs.label: E
